title: Arizona's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Arizona's 2nd Congressional District election is a rematch between incumbent Republican Representative Eli Crane and Democratic challenger Jonathan Nez, the former Navajo Nation President. Crane first won the seat in 2022 and was re-elected with 54.5% of the vote in 2024. The district covers more than half of Arizona, including Flagstaff, Prescott, and the Navajo Nation, making it geographically the largest district in the state with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+7. Key issues in the race include federal land management, tribal sovereignty, economic development, and the federal budget, with Nez criticizing Crane's votes against certain spending bills and Crane emphasizing his conservative record and military background.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Eli Crane
candidates.summary: Eli Crane is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A former U.S. Navy SEAL and co-founder of Bottle Breacher, Crane is a conservative Republican who has been endorsed by former President Donald Trump and the Club for Growth. He previously defeated Democratic incumbent Tom O'Halleran in 2022 and won re-election against Jonathan Nez in 2024.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race (zero polls as of June 2026), which limits precision. Incumbent Republican Eli Crane holds clear structural advantages: the district has a Cook PVI of R+7, Crane is the incumbent, and he defeated the same Democratic challenger, Jonathan Nez, in 2024 with 54.5% of the vote. Nez is a credible and previously tested opponent, preventing a 'safe' rating, but the district's partisan lean, coupled with Crane's incumbency and demonstrated electoral performance against Nez, gives the Republican a clear advantage. A 'likely R' rating (approximately 85% win probability, ~8-point margin) best reflects these conditions given the absence of polling.
